I've been growing cotton on this same Quzhou land for four decades. The soil here in the piedmont plain suits cotton — deep, well-drained loam. With only 2 mu more than a typical small plot and just the two of us in the household, I don't overcomplicate things. Cotton is what I know, and it still pays better than alternatives at my scale if managed right.

For seeds, I switched to hybrid varieties years ago and won't go back. The yield difference is real, and with my well I can support the crop fully through dry spells, which is when hybrid genetics pay off most.

I split fertilizer into a base application before planting and a topdress at the boll-development stage — nitrogen in particular needs to hit twice. I stay moderate on nitrogen; I've seen neighbors push it and get excessive vegetative growth that harms yield. Potassium matters for fiber quality, so I don't skimp there.

With well irrigation I run about 5 waterings: a pre-planting irrigation if the soil profile is dry, a light one at seedling establishment, one at flowering, one at peak boll set, and a final one if August turns hot and dry. I watch the sky and adjust — I don't irrigate on a fixed schedule like a younger farmer with less feel for the crop.

Bollworm, aphids, and spider mites are the recurring threats. I do 6 pesticide applications spread across the season, scouting before each decision. I use rotary tillage in spring — at 64, I've moved away from full ploughing unless the field is genuinely compacted.

I expect 320 kg/mu seed cotton. That's realistic for this county with proper inputs and timely irrigation.
